(a) Treatment.—Section 1965(10) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(C) The member’s stillborn child.”. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 101(4)(A) is amended by striking “section 1965(10)(B)” in the matter preceding clause (i) and inserting “subparagraph (B) or (C) of section 1965(10)”.

fable.w: This section only amends a statutory definition to add a member's stillborn child as an insurable dependent and makes a conforming cross-reference change. There is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Any tempting reading would rest on the fact that it relates to benefits, but benefit eligibility is not participation.
fable.s: Section 1965(10) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(C) The member’s stillborn child.”

opus.w: This section only changes a statutory definition by adding a member's stillborn child to the insurable dependents under section 1965(10), and updates a cross-reference to match. It creates no comment period, rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Words like "member" or "Treatment" do not create any process involving people outside the federal government, and who qualifies for benefits is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** This is a pure definitional amendment. It adds "the member's stillborn child" to the definition at 38 U.S.C. § 1965(10), which covers insurable dependents under servicemembers' group life insurance, and makes a matching cross-reference change in § 101(4)(A). The only tempting reading is a keyword one: "member" or "Treatment" might suggest an outside party or a process. But "member" means a service member, and nothing in the text has the government consult anyone, hold a hearing, take comments, issue rules, or allow a suit. Changing who counts as an eligible dependent is a benefits matter, which the definition excludes.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists solely of technical amendments to statutory definitions and cross-references regarding benefits for members' stillborn children. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or other forms of participation as defined. The text describes a change in eligibility criteria, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) Treatment.—Section 1965(10) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(C) The member’s stillborn child.”. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 101(4)(A) is amended by striking “section 1965(10)(B)” in the matter preceding clause (i) and inserting “subparagraph (B) or (C) of section 1965(10)”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending a statute to include "stillborn child" involves some public input or consultation, but the text itself is purely a legislative amendment to definitions and cross-references. It does not describe any process of consulting with outsiders, holding hearings, or creating advisory bodies. It is a substantive change to the law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
